Probir Neogi, Advocate—For the Accused-Petitioner. 
Snigdha Huq, Deputy Attorney-General with Sarah Parveen, Assistant Attorney-General—For the State.
parties:
Abdul Majid Fakir (Md) ------ Petitioner
Vs
State and ors ------ Opposite Parties.
full_judgment:
Mir Hashmat Ali J: In the instant Rule the opposite parties were asked to show cause as to why proceedings of Kamar Kahand PS Case No. 5 dated 18-1-2002 corresponding to GR Case No. 72 of 2002 now pending in the Court of Magistrate, 1st Class, Zone-Gha, Sirajganj arising out of order No. 3 dated 11-10-2001 and order No. 4 dated 31-10-2001 passed by Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Sirajganj in Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Case No. 523 of 2001 should not be quashed. 

 2. On a first information report lodged by present accused-petition; Abdul Majid Fakir, Kamar Kahand PS Case No. 3 dated 16- 7-2001 was started against the opposite-party Nos. 2-8 under section 5(1)/7/9(1)/30 of Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000. 

 6. According to the said direction, the police filed Kamar Kahand PS case No. 5 dated 18-1-2002 against the present accused-petitioner under section 17(1) of Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000. 

 9. The accused petitioner being aggrieved by the order dated 11-10-2001 and the proceedings against the accused-petitioner under section 17(1) of Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain by Kamar Kahand PS case No.5 dated 18-1-2002 GR case No.72 of 2002 preferred instant Miscellaneous application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained the Rule. 

 10. Mr Probir Neogi, the learned Advocate appearing with Md Mohammad Ali, Submits that the police before submission of final report did not examine the informant or victim nor the police took any steps to examine the victim by a medical expert for determining the offence of rape. The investigation officer never went to the place of occurrence nor examined any witnesses of the informant's party and the final report was submitted behind the back of the informant. The informant came to know of the final report after his arrest in a proceeding under section 17(1) of Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 on 31-10-2000 and instantly filed Naraji petition which is a fresh complaint petition but the Tribunal without considering the same and without complying with the provision of section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure summarily rejected the said complaint petition. He further submits that the Court on receipt of Naraji petition or a complaint petition is to examine the complainant on oath according to section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and on non examination of the complainant on oath, the order of rejection of the complaint petition is illegal and is not sustainable in law. In support of his contention, he cited the case of Nur Mohammad Mandal vs Md Abul Hossain and another reported 28 DLR 389. The learned Advocate further submits that the accused-persons even if discharged before the filing of the complaint petition or Naraji petition that discharge amounts to discharge from custody and not discharge from the case. He further submits that a Naraji petition is a fresh complaint and the Court is competent to take cognisance on the basis of Naraji petition on compliance of the formalities of the Code of Criminal Procedure and that such proceeding is not without jurisdiction of the Tribunal and, as such, the order dated 31-10-2001 passed by the Tribunal is misconceived and liable to he set aside. He further submits that the Tribunal had to consider the fact that the investigating officer never went to the place of occurrence and never examined any witness of the informant's party nor took any steps to examine the victim by any medical expert as it appears from the police report and that no alamat was seized nor any sketch map was made even the victim was not sent for medical examination and, as such, final report is perfunctory and it cannot be said that the informant accused petitioner filed a false case and, as such, subsequent proceeding against the accused-petitioner under section 17(1) of Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, of Kamar Kahand PS Case No. 5 dated 18-1-2002 GR case No.72 of 2002 is liable to be quashed. The learned Advocate further submits that the Tribunal has no authority to direct any other persons to initiate proceeding against the accused petitioner. In support of his contention he cited the case of Nurul Hug vs State reported in 55 DLR 588. 

 11. Mrs Sarah Parveen, the learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the State, found it difficult to oppose the Rule. She submits that after filing of Naraji petition or complaint petition, the Court or Tribunal is to examine the complainant on oath as required under section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in a case. 

 12. We have heard the learned Advocates of both the parties at length and miscellaneous application and the grounds thereunder and also the connected papers and documents annexed with the application. 

 13. It appears that the Magistrate sent the complaint petition to the police station and police treated the same as a first information report as Kamar Kahand PS case No.3 dated 16-7-2001 and started investigation though the investigation officer stated that he went to the place of occurrence and made sketch map and examined the witnesses, but from the investigation report and record we do not find that the victim was ever examined by the police or she was sent to the hospital for medical examination or police recovered any alamat or made any seizure list or sketch map. 

 15. It appears from the police report itself that on 14-3-2001 victim attempted to enter in to the house of the accused Md Helal Sheikh but father and mother and others objected to it for which she was standing in the street in front of the house of the accused-persons, witnesses came and heard about the occurrence subsequently. Liakat Ali and his wife took her to their house. There the respectable persons and UP member came and heard about the occurrence and informant and, as such, it appears from the police report itself that there was an occurrence which leads to the offence under section 5(1)/7/9(1) or section 30 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, whether the accused persons committed the offence is a matter of evidence to be decided at the time of trial. Without considering such aspect of the case, the Tribunal accepted the final report. The Tribunal in considering of the police report under section 173 of the Code of Criminal Procedure should not rely only upon the police report but the Tribunal or the Magistrate is to consider the whole case of the first information report, police report and the statements of the witnesses and also circumstances of the case and then to pass appropriate order. 

 16. From the order dated 11-10-2001 it appears that the Tribunal accepted the final report only on the misleading report and failed to consider the police report in all its aspects of the case and accepted the final report on the ground that no Naraji petition has been filed. Whether the informant files Naraji petition or not, that is not the vital point for consideration of the police report, the informant may or may not file Naraji petition but the Tribunal or the Magistrate is to consider the whole materials in its true perspective. 

 17. It appears from the order dated 31-10-2001 that the Court has already accepted the final report for which he has no jurisdiction to entertain a subsequent Naraji petition or complaint petition which is erroneous and misconceived. 

 18. It has been held in the case of Mind Huq vs Fazal Ahamed and 3 others reported in 48 DLR 327 that if an accused discharged from prosecution or on a final report that means that the accused has been discharged from custody, not discharged from the case and subsequent prosecution of the accused is permissible. It was further held in the said case that Naraji petition is a fresh complaint and a Magistrate is competent to take cognizance on the basis of a Naraji petition by complying with the requirements of the law. 

 19. In the instant case the Tribunal without examining the complainant on oath rejected the complaint petition. It has been held in the case of Nur Mohammad Mandal vs Abul Hossain and 3 others reported in 28 DLR 389 that the complainant is to be examined on oath under section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. We also held that without examining the complainant on oath, as required under section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, it cannot be determined as to whether there is a prima facie case against the accused-persons or not and without examining the complainant as required under section 200 of the Code the complaint petition cannot be thrown out in limine. 

 20. It appears from the record that after acceptance of final report Mr Shafiqur Rahman SI of Police Kamar Kahand police station filed a first information report, being Kamar Kahand PS Case No. 5 dated 18-1-2002 and arrested the petitioner and forwarded him on 23-1-2002 before the learned Magistrate. Since we have already held that the rejection of the complaint petition of the accused-petitioner dated 31-10-2001 is illegal the subsequent proceeding against the petitioner under section 17(1) of Nari-o-Shishu case cannot be continued which has been supported by the case of Nurul Huq (Md) vs State reported in 55 DLR 588, that the Tribunal cannot direct to initiate a proceeding. In the instant case the Tribunal directed the authority to initiate proceeding under section 17(1) of Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain on 11-10-2001 and, as such, the order dated 11-10-2001 passed by the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Bishes Adalat in Nari-o-Shishu case No.523 of 01 is not sustainable in law and initiating of such proceeding by the order dated 11-10-2001 cannot be sustained and continuation of such proceedings is an abuse of the process of the Court and liable to be quashed. 

 22. In the result, the Rule is made absolute, the impugned order No.3 dated 11-10-01 and order No.4 dated 31-10-01 passed by Nari-o-Shishu. Nirjatan case No.523 of 2001 is hereby set aside. The criminal proceedings of Kamarkahand PS case No.5 dated 18-1-2002 corresponding to GR case No.72 of 2002 now pending in the Court of Magistrate, 1st Class, Zone Gha, Sirajganj is hereby quashed. The accused petitioner, if on bail, be discharged from the bail bond if not wanted in any other case. The Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Sirajganj is directed to proceed with the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan case No.523 of 01 arising out of GR case No.351(GA) /01 Zone Gha, Kamar Kahand, PS case No.3 dated 16-7-01 in accordance with law.
